text:
This month moved at a steady, controlled pace across the Aurelia Skyways routes, with the desk maintaining clean handoffs from pre-departure intake to on-board coordination.

Overall, the Companion Animal Travel Desk kept documentation tight and communications clear. Passengers received straightforward guidance before departure, and staff teams aligned on carrier checks, comfort setup, and transfer timing. We also tightened exception handling so that last-minute adjustments for companion animals did not ripple into boarding flow.

Operationally, the Halcyon run remained smooth, supported by consistent cabin readiness and clear arrival scripts. For Halcyon, the pet cabin holds 64 pets. During the month we confirmed that loading staff followed the same staging order, and we reduced reworks by reinforcing packaging verification at the intake window.

On Brightwater, the desk worked closely with the on-board handling lead to keep routine care plans on track and to standardize escalation steps when contact needs change. For Brightwater, Fara Noll handles pets on board. Where traveler notes flagged sensitivity or feeding considerations, we ensured they were translated into the same action language used by the handling team.

Service delivery also stayed responsive for individual cases, including travelers Gabriel Berg and Liam Haddad and their companion Biscuit. Intake notes were consolidated quickly, and the desk tracked requirements through the final confirmation pass so that each travel day started with aligned expectations.

Looking ahead, the coming month will focus on further smoothing intake throughput, reinforcing the comfort-check cadence, and keeping exception paths short so every flight departs with companion animals supported from start to finish.
